heads/mha: In multi-head attention, each of h query heads has its own key head and value head. Here h is eight, each head sixty four numbers wide.
heads/cache: While generating, the KV cache keeps every earlier token's keys and values. Per token and layer, that is two, times h, times the head width: one thousand and twenty four numbers.
heads/big: Across every layer and every token of a long context, that adds up to gigabytes, all read again for every new token.
share/group: Grouped-query attention keeps all eight query heads, but only g key-value heads. With g at two, each key head and value head is shared by a group of four query heads.
share/attend: Each query head still makes its own scores and its own mix. It just reads the keys and values of its group.
share/shrink: The cache now holds two times g times sixty four: two hundred and fifty six numbers per token, four times smaller. It shrinks by h over g.
extremes/mha: At one extreme, g equals h: every query head has its own key and value head. That is ordinary multi-head attention, with the largest cache.
extremes/mqa: At the other, g is one: all the query heads share a single key head and value head, and the cache is h times smaller. That is multi-query attention, and it can cost some quality.
extremes/between: Grouped-query attention sits in between, close to multi-head quality at a fraction of the cache. Many large models keep eight key-value heads.
